# Detailed implementation plan: `lib/zaq/system.ex`

## Scope and evidence

Planning only; baseline supplied by coordinator: **94%**, missed lines **228, 628, 630, 644, 666, 720, 735, 736, 747, 765, 793, 804, 885, 889, 899**. Line numbers below are one-based and verified against live source. No tests or application commands were run. The plan predicts branch execution; it does not claim measured coverage or passing tests.

Loaded `test-coverage-planner`; read `AGENTS.md`, tool routing, testing handbook, system configuration service guide, applicable workflow/setup/documentation guidance. Used Serena overview and targeted symbols for System, Connect and mutation boundaries, then bounded reads for test macros, delegates and dependency transaction semantics. No production hooks or refactors are needed. **Action reuse: N/A — tests only, no executable operation changes.** No E2E is needed for these existing context contracts.

Read-only `bw prime` and issue listing found prior coverage work (`zaq-bcs`, `zaq-gda`, `zaq-k0t` closed; `zaq-5vh` in progress), but no specifically matching open System-context task in the filtered results. No Beadwork mutation is part of this plan. This temporary artifact is the user-requested handoff, not a new repository policy or durable tracker.

Dirty tree observed before and after inspection (all index-modified):

- `test/e2e/specs/system_config.spec.js`
- `test/e2e/support/bo.js`
- `test/e2e/support/people-auth-browser.cjs`
- `test/zaq_web/people_browser_test.exs`

Preserve these exactly. No Git mutations, repository code/test edits or execution occurred during planning.

## Ownership and sequence

| Test file | Ownership / isolation |
| --- | --- |
| `test/zaq/system/system_test.exs` (existing) | Numeric skill-source identifiers, scenario S1. Existing `Zaq.DataCase, async: false`; reuse its skill-resource describe block. |
| `test/zaq/system/ai_provider_runtime_resolution_test.exs` (new) | Router response-contract unit tests S2/S3. `ExUnit.Case, async: true`, process-private existing `Zaq.NodeRouterMock`, `setup :verify_on_exit!`; no database or global config. |
| `test/zaq/system/ai_provider_credential_test.exs` (existing) | S4–S10: canonical OAuth extraction, missing-association form fallback, transaction failures and encryption translation. Existing `Zaq.DataCase, async: false` and encryption setup. |
| `test/zaq/system/ai_provider_credential_transaction_test.exs` (new) | S11 only: System delete atomicity across a real Oban insertion failure. `Zaq.DataCase, async: false`; transaction-local DDL. |
| `test/zaq/system/outbound_http_policy_test.exs` (existing) | S12: blank list persistence and safe defaults. Existing `Zaq.DataCase, async: false`, existing property suite retained. |

Implementation order: add direct input/response cases S1–S5 and S12; then rollback/error cases S6–S10; then isolated DDL integration S11; coordinator runs `mix q` and focused tests. No subagents are required. Keep assertions on returned errors, persisted rows, grants and queued mutation events, never on private call order.

## Complete line map

| Line | Live branch | Planned proof |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 228 | `blank_to_nil/1` nonbinary pass-through | S1 numeric external scope/folder identifiers |
| 628 | Engine response `{:ok, nil}` | S2 exact unavailable error |
| 630 | Unexpected Engine response | S3 exact invalid-response wrapper |
| 644 | Resolved OAuth `access_token` becomes API-key compatibility result | S4 canonical org OAuth grant |
| 666 | Missing Connect association leaves form input unchanged | S5 unsaved struct with nonexistent integer association |
| 720 | AI creation transaction rolls back a changeset error | S6 duplicate AI name after Connect save; also S9 create encryption failure |
| 735 | AI update transaction rolls back a changeset error | S7 duplicate AI name after Connect changes; also S9 update encryption failure |
| 736 | AI update transaction translates an atomic Connect error | S8 unusable-global policy transition |
| 747 | Connect deletion error rolls back AI deletion | S11 real mutation-event enqueue failure |
| 765 | Legacy AI key encryption returns failed changeset | S9 OAuth/no-client-secret path with legacy API key and unavailable encryption configuration |
| 793 | Connect encryption failed but no AI API-key encryption failure exists to reuse | S10 OAuth client-secret encryption failure with absent AI API key |
| 804 | Generic Connect error becomes base changeset error | S10b invalid OAuth configuration |
| 885 | Blank one-argument string list | S12 persisted empty blacklist values |
| 889 | Blank string list with default | S12 persisted empty allowed methods |
| 899 | Blank integer list | S12 persisted empty allowed ports |

## Detailed scenarios

### S1 — numeric data-source identities survive storage normalization (228)

Owner: `system_test.exs`, describe `"skill resource config"`.

- Call `System.save_skill_resource_config(%{provider: "disk", config_id: 7, scope_id: 123, folder_id: 456, folder_path: " /knowledge "})`.
- Assert exact result `{:ok, %{provider: "disk", config_id: 7, scope_id: "123", folder_id: "456", folder_path: "/knowledge"}}`.
- Assert `System.get_skill_resource_config/0` equals the same map and `System.get_config("system.agent_skills.resources.scope_id") == "123"`, with analogous folder assertion.
- This exercises the nonbinary branch on normalized input, before `set_config/2` serializes scalars. Do not invent map/tuple inputs that fail `String.Chars` rather than test the supported scalar identity path.
- Add one bounded property alongside this example (`use ExUnitProperties` in the existing module): generate positive integer `scope_id` and `folder_id` in `1..1_000_000`, `max_runs: 25`; fixed provider/config/folder path. Invariant: saving numeric identities returns their decimal text; saving that returned map again is idempotent. Assert the two literal identity fields and exact second result. Conversion expectation is the public serialization contract, not a copied branch algorithm. Reuse the sandbox across property iterations; upsert fixed keys, no processes or randomness-sensitive assertions.

### S2 — Engine returns no credential (628)

Owner: new `ai_provider_runtime_resolution_test.exs`.

- Input `%AIProviderCredential{id: 42, connect_credential_id: 84}` (no DB insertion).
- `expect(Zaq.NodeRouterMock, :dispatch, fn %Zaq.Event{} = event -> ... end)`; assert `event.request == %{credential_id: 42}`, `event.next_hop.destination == :engine`, actor `%{kind: :system, subject: "system-ai-runtime"}`, `event.opts[:action] == :resolve_ai_runtime_credential`, `event.opts[:confidential] == true`.
- Return `%{event | response: {:ok, nil}}`.
- Invoke `System.resolve_ai_provider_authentication(credential, node_router_module: Zaq.NodeRouterMock)`.
- Assert exactly `{:error, %{credential_id: nil, reason: :credential_unavailable}}`. The nil ID is the current contract, not 42 or 84.

### S3 — malformed Engine response is rejected (630)

Same owner and mock discipline as S2. Use separate generated example tests for two deliberate response shapes: `{:ok, %{credential: %{id: 42}}}` (missing resolved credential) and `:unexpected_response` (wrong envelope). Return each as `event.response`; assert exact `{:error, {:invalid_runtime_credential_response, supplied_response}}`. Each test owns one private expectation and verifies the confidential event fields above. No global router override and no blanket stubs. Existing success/unavailability tests in `ai_provider_credential_test.exs:364–404` remain their current owners; do not copy their happy-path cases.

### S4 — compatibility API returns the canonical OAuth access token (644)

Owner: existing `ai_provider_credential_test.exs`.

1. Create a unique AI row through `System.create_ai_provider_credential/1`: provider `"openai"`, endpoint `"https://api.openai.com/v1"`, metadata `%{"auth_kind" => "oauth2", "client_id" => "client-id"}`. Default OAuth personal policy is required; no grant initially.
2. Call `Connect.replace_credential_grant(ai.connect_credential_id, :org, %{access_token: "canonical-oauth-access", refresh_token: "canonical-oauth-refresh", expires_at: ~U[2099-01-01 00:00:00Z]})` and assert success.
3. Reload AI via `System.get_ai_provider_credential!/1`; assert `System.resolve_ai_provider_api_key(ai) == "canonical-oauth-access"`. Explicitly refute equality with `"canonical-oauth-refresh"`.
4. Optionally assert the resolved credential's `credential_id` is the associated Connect ID, `owner_type == "org"`, `auth_kind == "oauth2"`, and `authentication == %{access_token: "canonical-oauth-access"}` in this same thin integration test. Do not add a second equivalent resolver test.

Use real NodeRouter/Engine/Connect resolution as existing tests do. Future expiry avoids refresh and all provider HTTP. No OpenAI stub or Factory runtime is required. Do not use existing `issue_connect_ai_grant/3`: it deliberately creates a **legacy resource-bound** grant and cannot reach this branch through canonical resolution. Avoid logging secret-bearing results.

### S5 — form changeset preserves policy when association is unavailable (666)

Owner: existing `ai_provider_credential_test.exs`.

- Establish `Connect.fetch_credential(-1) == {:error, :not_found}`.
- Build an unsaved `%AIProviderCredential{name: "Missing association", provider: "openai", endpoint: "https://api.openai.com/v1", connect_credential_id: -1, personal_credential_policy: :required}`.
- Call `System.change_ai_provider_credential(input, %{description: "editable description"})`.
- Assert `changeset.data == input`, `get_field(changeset, :personal_credential_policy) == :required`, `get_field(changeset, :connect_credential_id) == -1`, and `get_change(changeset, :description) == "editable description"`.
- This is a public form builder accepting a stale/unpersisted reference, not a persisted FK violation. Never disable FK constraints or delete a referenced Connect row to arrange it.

### S6 — AI uniqueness failure rolls back a newly created Connect definition (720)

Owner: existing `ai_provider_credential_test.exs`.

Arrange using public operations so the failure occurs at the AI insert, not Connect's own name uniqueness check:

1. Create no-auth AI with unique name `original_name`, explicit metadata `%{"auth_kind" => "none"}`.
2. Rename it with `System.update_ai_provider_credential(existing, %{name: target_name})`. Verify its associated Connect name remains `"AI: #{original_name}"`; configuration adapter preserves the existing Connect name.
3. Capture notification job IDs after arrangement.
4. Attempt to create another no-auth AI named `target_name` with valid provider/endpoint. `"AI: #{target_name}"` is unused, so Connect creation succeeds before AI name uniqueness fails.
5. Assert `{:error, %Ecto.Changeset{} = cs}`, `errors_on(cs).name == ["has already been taken"]`, and `cs.data.__struct__ == AIProviderCredential`.
6. Assert exactly the original AI remains under `target_name`, `Connect` has no credential named `"AI: #{target_name}"`, and mutation notification job IDs equal the pre-call snapshot. Original Connect and its association remain intact.

Use short UUID-suffixed names below 255 bytes. No artificial database index or internal module stub is needed.

### S7 — AI update uniqueness failure rolls back preceding Connect changes (735)

Owner: existing `ai_provider_credential_test.exs`.

- Create distinct no-auth AI A and B with unique names. Capture B's Connect row, AI fields and mutation job IDs.
- Update B with `%{name: a.name, provider: "anthropic", endpoint: "https://api.anthropic.com/v1"}`. The initial AI changeset is valid; Connect's provider mutation occurs before AI name uniqueness is checked on UPDATE.
- Assert returned AI changeset has exact `name` uniqueness message.
- Reload B: name, provider, endpoint and `connect_credential_id` equal original values. Reload its Connect row: provider and name equal originals. A still exists with its original values. Notification job IDs equal the pre-call snapshot.
- This verifies atomic rollback across both persisted records, rather than only the returned changeset.

### S8 — invalid policy transition translates an update error and remains atomic (736)

Owner: existing `ai_provider_credential_test.exs`.

- Create valid `"openai"` AI with `personal_credential_policy: :required`, no API key and no metadata override. Call the public create function directly: the generic fixture would silently select explicit no-auth for an absent key.
- Assert associated Connect policy is `:required` and `Connect.list_grants(credential_id: connect_id) == []`.
- Capture AI description and notification job IDs.
- Update with `%{personal_credential_policy: :optional, description: "must roll back"}`.
- Assert changeset base errors include exactly the established message `"a usable global credential is required for disabled or optional personal credentials"`.
- Reload: policy remains `:required`, grant list remains empty, description is unchanged, association unchanged, notification job IDs unchanged.
- Do not assert the error changeset is otherwise valid or contains no other fields: `ai_credential_error/2` builds from submitted attrs on a fresh schema and partial updates can also carry required-field errors.

### S9 — legacy AI key encryption fails after valid Connect configuration (765; 720 or 735)

Owner: existing `ai_provider_credential_test.exs`, its serialized encryption setup.

Why the ordinary API-key case does not prove this branch: canonical API-key grant encryption fails earlier inside Connect. To reach `save_ai_provider_credential/2`, use valid OAuth configuration with no client secret; OAuth ignores the retained legacy AI `api_key` for canonical auth.

Two focused examples:

**Create:** set `Application.put_env(:zaq, Zaq.System.SecretConfig, encryption_key: nil, key_id: "test-v1")` in a scoped helper/try-after. Create unique AI with normal provider/endpoint, `api_key: "legacy-key-must-not-persist"`, metadata `%{"auth_kind" => "oauth2", "client_id" => "client-id"}`, policy `:required`. Connect can create its secret-free configuration and remove absent org grant; then AI legacy-key encryption fails. Assert exact API-key error `"could not be encrypted: missing SYSTEM_CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY"`, no change for `:api_key` remains, no AI row, no `"AI: #{name}"` Connect row, and no new mutation jobs.

**Update:** first create the same valid secret-free OAuth row under the normal test key. Snapshot AI, Connect and jobs. Switch to missing-key configuration and update `%{endpoint: "https://api.openai.com/v2", api_key: "legacy-update-must-not-persist"}`. Assert the same exact API-key error; restore encryption config before loading encrypted schemas. AI endpoint/key/association and Connect configuration remain original; no new jobs. This reaches 765 → 735 without a secret race or mock.

Do not assert a supported canonical API-key authentication mode for the legacy field: the purpose is strict failure/rollback of the compatibility write. If a future version rejects simultaneous OAuth metadata and legacy key earlier, record 765 as no longer reachable via this scenario; do not add a bypass or test-only hook.

### S10 — OAuth client-secret encryption error uses generic AI-key message (793)

Owner: existing `ai_provider_credential_test.exs`.

- With missing encryption config, submit unique valid provider/name/endpoint plus metadata `%{"auth_kind" => "oauth2", "client_id" => "client-id", "client_secret" => "client-secret-must-not-persist"}` and no `api_key`.
- Connect validates OAuth config, then fails encrypting `client_secret`, returning `:encryption_failed`.
- System's error mapper has no AI API-key change; its encryption check returns `:skip`, reaching line 793.
- Assert `errors_on(cs).api_key == ["could not be encrypted"]`, no AI row or generated Connect row, and unchanged notification job IDs.
- Do not assert a missing-encryption-key-specific message here: the field whose encryption failed belongs to Connect and this branch intentionally supplies the generic System message.
- Do not dump metadata/changesets to logs; unlike the API-key removal case, this plan does not assume arbitrary AI metadata inspection is redacted.

### S10b — invalid OAuth configuration maps to a fixed base error (804)

Same owner; valid normal encryption setup.

- Create input: unique valid AI name, `provider: "openai"`, normal endpoint, metadata `%{"auth_kind" => "oauth2"}` with **no client_id**.
- AI schema accepts the metadata and reaches Connect; Connect's candidate changeset requires a client ID and returns `:invalid_configuration`.
- Assert `cs.errors[:base]` matches `{"authentication configuration is invalid", metadata}` and `metadata[:reason] == :invalid_configuration`. Assert no AI row, no generated Connect row and unchanged jobs.
- Do not use an unknown `auth_kind`: the configuration adapter's function clauses would raise before this error mapping, testing a different contract.

### S11 — Connect delete enqueue failure restores the AI and Connect pair (747)

Owner: new `ai_provider_credential_transaction_test.exs`.

1. Use `Zaq.DataCase, async: false`. Reuse `SystemConfigFixtures.ai_credential_fixture/1` with explicit no-auth to create a valid AI + Connect pair, avoiding encryption-global setup. For the minimal required case there is no grant; assert the pair's persistence. A grant-bearing expansion is unnecessary because Connect's existing transaction tests own grant cascade restoration.
2. Assert none of `llm.credential_id`, `embedding.credential_id`, `image_to_text.credential_id` references this AI. Capture the relevant notification job IDs.
3. After setup succeeds, execute transaction-local DDL matching `test/zaq/engine/connect/mutation_event_transaction_test.exs:9–12`:
   `ALTER TABLE oban_jobs ADD CONSTRAINT system_ai_delete_event_failure CHECK (queue <> 'connect_credential_notifications') NOT VALID`.
4. Call `System.delete_ai_provider_credential(ai)`; assert exactly `{:error, :mutation_event_enqueue_failed}`.
5. Reload AI and Connect, assert both IDs/association and their original field values still exist; no deletion notification job was added. The initial AI `Repo.delete!` must be rolled back with Connect's deletion.

This is a genuine DB/Oban failure seam, not a mock of Connect. Existing `MutationEvents.delete/1` catches enqueue errors as rollback reasons; DBConnection's nested `transaction/3` returns `{:error, reason}` after a nested rollback, allowing System's line 747 to run. Sandbox rollback removes the DDL constraint at test teardown. Never call migrations, globally stop Oban, replace the repo module, or install a trigger. Keep this file serialized and run its focused command separately when other schema-changing suites are being coordinated.

### S12 — persisted empty policy lists use safe defaults (885, 889, 899)

Owner: existing `outbound_http_policy_test.exs`, System describe block.

Important existing-test gap: `"falls back safely for empty and malformed list settings"` writes multiple values to the same keys and only reads once; blank hosts/ports are overwritten. Also, `Config.changeset/2` converts a first blank insert to nil, while `set_config/2`'s conflict update stores the literal empty string. Merely adding `set_config(key, "")` for a new key does not reliably exercise these three lines.

Add one explicit transition test:

- Seed these keys through `System.set_config/2` with nonempty JSON values: `blacklisted_hosts = ["blocked.example"]`, `blacklisted_ips = ["10.0.0.2"]`, `blacklisted_cidrs = ["10.0.0.0/8"]`, `allowed_methods = ["POST"]`, `allowed_ports = [8443]` (JSON strings).
- Set all five keys to `""` using `set_config/2` again, exercising the real public upsert clear operation. Assert each `System.get_config(key) == ""` before the policy read; this is the branch precondition and protects against an accidental NULL fixture.
- Read `policy = System.get_outbound_http_policy()` once. Assert all three blacklists equal `[]`, `allowed_methods == ~w(GET HEAD OPTIONS)`, `allowed_ports == []`. Also assert defaults `enabled == false` and `follow_redirects == false` remain fail-closed.
- Keep the existing scalar JSON property and mixed-port example. If improving the old fallback test, assert immediately after each table entry instead of asserting only after overwrites; do not remove its malformed JSON cases. No extra normalization property is needed here because existing property coverage already owns malformed scalar fallbacks.

## Helpers, mocks and isolation details

- Reuse `Zaq.DataCase` sandbox and `errors_on/1`. It uses shared sandbox mode for `async: false`; keep shared-state and DDL scenarios serialized. All calls here are synchronous; no sleeps, polling, worker drains, timers or Task coordination are needed.
- Reuse `SystemConfigFixtures.ai_credential_fixture/1` only when its explicit authentication selection preserves the scenario (not S8). Direct input maps are clearer for failure cases. Do not seed LLM/embedding configuration; unrelated chunk-table lifecycle is not part of this plan.
- Existing `RuntimeCredentialRouter` in `ai_provider_credential_test.exs` already owns successful/confidential and Engine-unavailable cases. New pure response tests can use the existing behavior-backed `Zaq.NodeRouterMock` declared once in `test/support/mocks.ex:2`, with per-test exact expectations and `verify_on_exit!`. No new support mock, Mox global mode or config mutation is needed.
- Existing `Zaq.TestSupport.ConnectEncryptionConfig` supports per-call overrides at Connect boundaries, but System's create/update entry points do not thread encryption opts. Do not pretend that helper can control System encryption. S9/S10 therefore use the existing isolated application-environment seam. Capture `Application.fetch_env/2`, restore the exact prior presence/value using put/delete in `after`; register an on-exit safeguard. Restore immediately before any later encrypted reload. Do not change OS environment or invoke external networks.
- Existing credential module's setup itself snapshots with a default list; if touching that setup, preserve absent-vs-present semantics with `fetch_env`/delete rather than expanding global scope. Keep tests in the existing serialized module; do not make the new pure runtime module a DataCase just for fixture convenience.
- Repeated rollback assertions may justify one **local** helper returning sorted IDs from `Oban.Job` where `queue == "connect_credential_notifications"`; use it before/after each operation. Do not drain jobs, assert incidental ordering, or compare random event IDs to literals. For single-use DDL, keep SQL inline or local; do not create a shared failure-injection framework.
- For AI/Connect rollback compare a selected field projection and ID, not random ciphertext regeneration or incidental timestamps. When encryption state is unavailable, use raw SQL only if essential to compare stored bytes; ordinary no-secret rows and restored-key reads suffice in the planned cases.

## Overlap and implementation coordination

**Migration ownership:** `test/zaq/system/ai_provider_credential_migration_test.exs` owns classification, ambiguous legacy OAuth grants, unreadable keys and keyset pagination. `ai_provider_credential_backfill_migration_test.exs` owns actual schema/backfill/rollback and retained encrypted material. S4 and S9 overlap conceptually with OAuth/legacy-key handling but test current System runtime/write contracts; do not replay migrations or add backfill cases for these lines. The backfill suite performs DDL and must not run concurrently with S11 in separate Mix processes sharing a DB.

**Provider ownership:** `test/zaq/agent/provider_spec_test.exs:543–561` already verifies canonical grant authority over a legacy AI key; `579–601` owns Codex token option translation. S4 needs only the System compatibility accessor, not another ProviderSpec test. Provider configuration fixture changes by another task can affect both suites; coordinate any support-file edit rather than modifying shared fixtures for this plan.

**Factory ownership:** `test/zaq/agent/factory_test.exs:37–203` already owns actor-aware runtime credential resolution, confidential Engine dispatch and Engine unavailability. Its later tests own runtime construction/LLM options. S2/S3 test System's response interpretation, not Factory lifecycle or Person selection. Do not add Factory integration runs, tool loops or runtime mock branches to reach these System lines.

**Connect ownership:** `test/zaq/engine/connect/mutation_event_transaction_test.exs` already forces real Oban errors and checks Connect rollback. S11 adds only the missing outer System transaction (AI deletion restored with Connect). Reuse the failure technique, not its broad mutation matrix. Canonical refresh, Person policy semantics and secret encryption implementation remain existing owners' responsibility.

## Reachability and exception policy

No requested line is currently proven unreachable. All 15 have a concrete public-call path above. Execution is still required to verify predictions.

- 666 is unreachable via a *valid persisted missing FK*, but reachable through the public form changeset on an unsaved/stale struct; no schema corruption is required.
- 765 is normally preempted by Connect encryption for canonical API-key writes. OAuth with no client secret permits a legacy-key persistence failure after canonical configuration, so it is not inherently dead.
- 793 is not reached by repeating the existing API-key missing-key test; it requires a different encrypted field (OAuth client secret) while the AI API key is absent.
- 747's `:not_found` collaborator outcome is not a reliable scenario: System first loads the row and a disappearance would require a race. The deterministic enqueue-failure path is the intended test instead.
- 885/889/899 require literal stored empty strings, not NULL, missing rows, malformed JSON, or empty JSON lists. S12 arranges the real upsert transition precisely.

If focused execution disproves a path, report the exact earlier branch/error and its public preconditions to the coordinator. Do not weaken assertions, mock System/Repo/Connect internals, use module redefinition, manipulate global keys mid-operation, or manufacture concurrent races. A remaining defensive branch may be documented as an exception only after that evidence; do not promise 100% coverage now or add coverage-ignore directives.

## Coordinator-only focused validation commands

These are proposed commands, **not executed by the planner**. Run from repository root with the existing isolated test database/configuration. Keep each command's output in Context Mode. Run sequentially; especially do not overlap DDL/global-encryption suites with independent Mix jobs.

1. `mix q`
2. `mix test test/zaq/system/ai_provider_runtime_resolution_test.exs`
3. `mix test test/zaq/system/system_test.exs test/zaq/system/outbound_http_policy_test.exs`
4. `mix test test/zaq/system/ai_provider_credential_test.exs`
5. `mix test test/zaq/system/ai_provider_credential_transaction_test.exs test/zaq/engine/connect/mutation_event_transaction_test.exs`

No separate formatting command (`mix q` includes it), `mix precommit`, full suite, E2E, migration replay or broad coverage command is assigned here. Provider/Factory/migration overlap is flagged for coordination, not an automatic instruction to broaden testing. After edits, use the new test declaration line numbers for single-case reruns only when investigating a failure. Run each successful check once unless changes/failures justify a repeat.

Completion report should name changed test files, targeted command results and any evidence-backed branch exception. Preserve the coordinator's supplied 94% as an unverified baseline; numerical improvement requires a separately authorized coverage measurement. No production changes are needed to implement this plan.


Coordinator execution override: tests only in assigned files, preserve pre-existing edits; no worker Mix/Git/Beadwork mutations. Coordinator alone runs mix q and added/edited tests --cover. No full-suite or precommit execution for this coverage task.
